## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `--exclude` flag should take its default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE`, because the project's CLI-flag policy requires an environment default for every newly added flag. This review found no other defect in the exclusion logic or the added tests, which were read and not run.

## Changes
The pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag to `cli/main.py` that skips files whose base name matches any pattern during collection. It also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md`, adds five tests, and adds a fixture file `tests/fixtures/hostile-review.txt`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the `--exclude` default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` — Running with `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE='*.log'` set and no `--exclude` argument still archives `.log` files, because the default is the literal `[]`. `.claude/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11` requires: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable". — CI jobs that set options through the environment cannot apply exclusions, so files they meant to skip end up in the archive. — Fix: Choose and document a separator for multiple globs in `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE`, record the variable in `docs/flags.md:7`, and extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing` to cover it.
